name_reason: Compliant with global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix + battle domain + _count descriptor (reflects an integer counter). No Ghidra address residue. The descriptor reads slightly narrow (it counts ALL teams in the runtime_char roster -- player team 2, enemy team 0, NPC team 1 -- not only the player's party), but it is the established, consistent name used across every reader/writer and matches sibling plate comments; the refined comment now states the full-roster scope, so no rename is warranted.
purpose: Total number of occupied runtime_char slots in the current battle (the full character roster across all teams), used as the 0..count loop bound over data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr and as that array's element count.
logic_summary: Established at chapter/save load time, then read throughout the battle. Writers: (1) fd2_load_chapter_battle_data @ 0x1099A sets it = data_fd2_resource_portrait_cache_total_size (the FDFIELD.DAT tile_event_data_table[1] count) then loops 0..count filling each runtime_char slot (active slots copied from the menu roster, others memset+dead-marked); (2) fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @ 0x1029A sets it = pBuf[0x30C4] (saved count from FD2.SAV +0x30C4), then memmove's count*0x50 bytes into runtime_char_array and rebuilds portrait sprites for 0..count; (3) fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle @ 0x1100B uses it as the append index (runtime_char_array + count) then post-increments (INC). Many readers iterate for(i=0;i<count;i++) over runtime_char_array[i] (e.g. fd2_check_battle_end_condition tests bTeam==0 to find enemies, confirming the array/count spans all teams). Value is widened from a byte at write time and consumed signed as a loop bound.
datatype: uint32 (4-byte counter; signed at loop-bound use sites, stored at full dword width; BSS zero-init)
element_semantics: Scalar counter: count of occupied 0x50-byte runtime_char entries in data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr for the active battle, spanning player (team 2), enemy (team 0) and NPC (team 1) characters.
comment_original_issue: Existing src comment block was accurate and detailed (purpose, all 3 writers, width rationale, BSS) but its opening described the value as 'number of runtime_char slots in the active battle party', which reads as the player's party only; the count actually spans the full roster across all teams (readers test bTeam to distinguish enemies).
notes: Ghidra data PLATE_COMMENT at 0x53BEB was null; created a concise plate (817 chars) via run_script_inline + CodeUnit.PLATE_COMMENT reflecting the src conclusion (full-roster scope, 3 writers, uint32 rationale). src comment opening sentence augmented to state the all-teams scope. No logic/equivalence concerns found. read_memory shows all-zero (BSS). name kept (convention-compliant, no address residue).
